description: Paper-canonical result CSVs backing every number and figure in the ICNLSP 2026 submission. Each entry pins the sha256 of the file as it was used for the final camera-ready. Files here are FROZEN — the sha256s WILL NOT match after a re-run because eval CSVs contain a wall-clock `elapsed_s` column and numerical differences across GPU hardware, drivers, CUDA/cuBLAS versions, and discrete decoding decisions can change exact WER values. Re-runs should preserve all frozen columns (new diagnostic columns may be added), cohort, and row order; compare numerical results against the frozen artifacts and report observed differences rather than assuming a universal WER tolerance (see docs/REPRODUCE.md).

paper.title: Token Merging for Multilingual Speech Recognition: A Systematic Study Across Model Scale and Fine-Tuning

files.name: fixed_rate_main_rerun_cfgA_n264_halfall_single.csv
files.notes: Main sweep on 18 mid/low/very-low-resource languages at TRRs {0, .05, .10, .20, .30, .40}. The paper plots the 12-language subset in `langs_plotted` (matches `main_sweep_12` under `paper.cohort`); the other 6 rows (am_et, pa_in, sn_zw, so_so, uz_uz, yo_ng) were collected in the same run but excluded from Table 2 / Figure 2 for cohort-consistency reasons. Cited numbers (over the 12 plotted langs at TRR=0.40): mean Delta-WER = -0.21 pp; worst degradation = +1.01 pp (sw_ke); largest improvement = -1.41 pp (ln_cd). Recomputing over all 18 rows will not reproduce those exact numbers.

files.name: whisper_size_baseline_whisper-medium_n264_medium_highres.csv
files.notes: Medium-model anchor sweep. Contains 5 high-resource languages (en, es, de, fr, cmn); the paper's Figure 2 top and Table 2 anchor row use the 4-language subset in `langs_plotted` (en/es/de/fr) — Mandarin was collected in the same run but excluded to keep the anchor cohort aligned with the cross-scale plots in Figure 3.

files.name: whisper_size_baseline_whisper-small_n264_mix16.csv
files.notes: Full 16-lang cross-scale sweep on whisper-small (244M, 12 enc layers). Mean Delta-WER on trained-6 at TRR=0.40 = +0.08 pp.

files.notes: Canonical merged 16-lang cross-scale sweep on whisper-large-v3 (1.55B, 32 enc layers). Mean Delta-WER on trained-6 at TRR=0.40 = +0.32 pp; worst +1.65 (Javanese).

paper_refs: Figure 3 (loaded via fig3_cross_scale_ft.py which concatenates both shards)

files.name: finetune_merge_rerun_cfgA_n264_checkpoint-2000_mix6.csv
files.notes: Merging sweep applied on top of the DoRA-adapted model. Max cost at TRR=0.40 = +0.59 pp (Lingala). Fine-tuned WER improvements over stock medium: Lingala -31 pp, Javanese -16 pp, Hausa -13 pp, Maltese -6 pp; Vietnamese + Tamil unchanged.

files.name: finetune_holdout_cfgA_n264_checkpoint-2000_mix6.csv
files.notes: Merging + DoRA evaluated on 10 held-out languages (4 anchors + 6 untrained mid/low). Anchors preserved (+0.02 pp mean drift from FT). Untrained drift +1.77 pp mean, max +3.78 (kk_kz). Merging still cheap: mean +0.23 pp, max +0.97 (Icelandic).

files.name: layer_similarity_whisper-small_n264.csv
files.notes: Per-layer mean head-averaged K-cosine similarity across 16 langs, forward-pass only (no decoding).

files.name: layer_similarity_whisper-medium_n264.csv
files.notes: Regenerated on all 16 langs. Per-layer means differ <0.4% from the earlier 11-lang cohort — structural invariance validated.

files.name: theoretical_flops_summary.csv
files.notes: Per-model encoder FLOP reductions at TRR=0.40: small 24.6%, medium 24.3%, DoRA 24.3%, large-v3 25.1%. Analytic, no GPU required. Regenerated from the eight source *_with_flops.csv sidecars produced by `tmm_asr.eval.flops` over the current release CSVs (mix6 / mix16); historical filenames like medium_stock_6FT and large_v3_func5 are no longer referenced.
